name: Run a treasury or Convex operation
description: Njord only. Runs a treasury operation as you, or one Convex operation as a user of this venue. Treasury operations take no `user`: v/ops/treasury/account-list, budget-list, ledger (reads), account-add, budget-create {id, account, amount, purpose?}, budget-lower {id, amount}, budget-cancel {id}, pay {budget, recipient, amount, reason}; each is granted exactly the account or budget it names, and an account's limit is the owner's to set. Convex operations sign with a key from that user's own secret store and need `user`: njord--treasury for your treasury, where your keys live and no one else can use them, or another user DID of this venue (user:sudo) when the owner's own key is to be used. Convex operations: v/ops/convex/query {source, address?, peer?} (free read; an address it runs as must hold a balance; leave it out to read without one), v/ops/secret/list (key names, never values), v/ops/convex/generate-key {name} (in your treasury only; returns the new account key, never the seed; the account itself is created and funded from an existing holder), v/ops/convex/sign {seed: s/NAME, message}, v/ops/convex/transact {address, source, seed: s/NAME, peer?}. peer is host:port; without it a query or transaction goes to the public Convex network. A seed goes by secret reference only; a literal one is refused. Without `user`, v/ops/job/cancel with the `id` of an Inbox request Njord made itself withdraws it, once it no longer needs an answer; no other job. Anything else is refused. Anything that changes state or signs needs `reason`, and is reported to Odin with its input and outcome as soon as it is done; the output then carries report {address, id}. Every run is a recorded job.

operation.description: The full operation path, e.g. v/ops/convex/transact.

input.description: The operation's own input, exactly as its schema describes. Keys go by reference (s/NAME), never as a literal seed.

user.description: For a Convex operation: njord--treasury for your treasury, or a user DID of this venue. Left out for a treasury operation.

reason.description: Required for anything that changes state or signs: your ledger line — what is paid, to whom, and on what authority. Odin receives it with the outcome. Up to 2000 characters.

output.description: The operation's own output; after a change, with report {address, id}: the task that told Odin. A query or transaction gives the network's result: value, or errorCode when the network refused it or it failed — then nothing moved, though a transaction that ran still cost its fee. info.tx is a transaction's hash.
